title: Preparedness in practice: kits, plans, drills and early warning

say: Preparedness in practice: kits, plans, drills and early warning.
This is the video for module two of Disaster Risk Management and Recovery.
An emergency kit has two parts. The home kit keeps your household going for at least three days. The grab bag is a ready-packed bag you can pick up in under a minute.

panel.heading: Turn your audit into protection
items: A home kit for at least 3 days
A grab bag you can lift in a minute

say: Then you need a practised plan, and a warning that reaches everyone in time.

panel.heading: Turn your audit into protection
items: A home kit for at least 3 days

say: Plan about 4 litres of water per person per day, for 3 days.

panel.heading: Work out your water and food
items: Water: people x 4 litres x 3 days
Food: 2 meals a day, little cooking

say: For example, Blessing in Lokoja has six people at home. 6 times 4 times 3 is 72 litres. Three 25-litre jerrycans with tight lids hold 75 litres.

panel.heading: Work out your water and food
items: Water: people x 4 litres x 3 days
Food: 2 meals a day, little cooking

say: For food she plans 2 simple meals a day, 36 portions, that need little or no cooking, like garri, groundnuts and ring-pull tins.

panel.heading: Work out your water and food
items: Water: people x 4 litres x 3 days
Food: 2 meals a day, little cooking

say: She dates each jerrycan and refills them every 3 months.

panel.heading: Work out your water and food
items: Water: people x 4 litres x 3 days
Food: 2 meals a day, little cooking

say: Use clean, food-grade containers with lids, never ones that held fuel or chemicals. Throw away swollen, rusty or dented tins.

panel.heading: Work out your water and food
items: Water: people x 4 litres x 3 days

panel.rule: Food-grade containers only. Never ones that held fuel or chemicals.

say: Copies of NIN slips, birth certificates and land papers, sealed in two zip bags. You need them to register for relief.

panel.heading: What goes in the grab bag
items: Document copies in two zip bags

say: A paper phone list, because phones die. Include SEMA or LEMA, and 112. And cash in small notes, because POS may be down.

panel.heading: What goes in the grab bag
items: Document copies in two zip bags

say: A charged power bank, a torch and a whistle, which carries further than a voice.

panel.heading: What goes in the grab bag
items: Document copies in two zip bags

say: Medicines with a card naming each one, pads, clothes and baby items for every person. If money is tight, build the kit over four weeks.

panel.heading: What goes in the grab bag
items: Document copies in two zip bags

say: A plan is a set of decisions made calmly, in advance. Agree the trigger, a safe destination on higher ground, and two routes, both walked on foot.

panel.heading: Decide calmly, in advance
items: A named helper for each person in need
Return only when authorities say safe

say: Agree meeting points, and roles: who takes the grab bag, and who switches off gas and electricity.

panel.heading: Decide calmly, in advance
items: A named helper for each person in need
Return only when authorities say safe

say: Give every child, older person, pregnant woman or person with disability a named helper and a back-up. Return only when authorities say it is safe.

panel.heading: Decide calmly, in advance
items: A named helper for each person in need
Return only when authorities say safe

say: In a flood, move people to higher ground early. Switch off electricity at the mains only if you and the floor are dry.
If you smell gas, close the cylinder valve if safe, open doors and windows, get everyone out, and call for help from outside.

panel.heading: Flood and gas: do and do not
left: Switch off mains only if you are dry
Gas smell: close valve, open windows
Get everyone out, call from outside
right: Walk or drive through moving water
Touch switches when you smell gas
Use a phone near a gas leak

say: Never walk or drive through moving water. About 15 cm can knock you down, and about 30 cm can sweep a vehicle away.
When you smell gas, do not touch switches, do not use a phone near the leak, and do not light a flame.

say: If fire starts, shout, get out low under smoke, close doors behind you, and call 112. Never go back for belongings, and never throw water on burning oil.

panel.heading: Fire and generator fumes

cards.d: Shout, get out low under smoke, close doors, meet outside, call 112. Never go back in.
Stop, drop to the ground, cover the face and roll. Do not run.
Outdoors only, away from doors and windows. Its fumes can kill sleeping people.

say: If clothes catch fire: stop, drop, cover the face and roll. Running feeds the flames.

say: Never run a generator inside a room, corridor or shop, even with a window open. Its exhaust contains carbon monoxide, a gas you cannot see or smell.

say: For example, Rukayat in Ibadan timed a flood drill with her household of five. The first try took 9 minutes 40 seconds.

panel.heading: Time a drill, fix it, drill again
items: Start a timer and say: flood alert, go

say: The torch was in another room, nobody knew who carried the grab bag, and her father's shoes were not by the door. She fixed all three, for free.

panel.heading: Time a drill, fix it, drill again
items: Start a timer and say: flood alert, go

say: A week later the drill took 5 minutes 50 seconds, about 40 percent faster.

panel.heading: Time a drill, fix it, drill again
items: Start a timer and say: flood alert, go

say: Write the date, the time and what changed.

panel.heading: Time a drill, fix it, drill again
items: Start a timer and say: flood alert, go
panel.rule: Drill at least twice a year: before the rains and before harmattan.

say: A forecast nobody hears saves no one. If one person calls 60 households at a minute each, that takes 60 minutes.

panel.heading: A phone tree for 60 households
items: Each captain calls 12 homes at once
Name a back-up for every captain

say: Instead, the warning lead calls 5 street captains, and each captain calls 12 households at the same time. That is about 17 minutes.

panel.heading: A phone tree for 60 households
items: Each captain calls 12 homes at once
Name a back-up for every captain

say: Name a back-up for each captain in case a phone is off. Say who the message is from, what is happening, and what to do now.

panel.heading: A phone tree for 60 households
items: Each captain calls 12 homes at once
Name a back-up for every captain

say: Send a warning only when it is confirmed. Too many false alarms make people ignore the real one.

panel.heading: A phone tree for 60 households

panel.rule: Confirm the alert first. Label every test as a test.

say: To remember. Store water for 3 days, and keep a grab bag ready. Never cross moving water, never run a generator indoors, and never touch switches when you smell gas. Time your drills, and warn fast with a phone tree.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Water: people x 4 litres x 3 days
Grab bag: papers, cash, light, medicines
Generators outdoors; no switches near gas
Time drills; use a phone tree with back-ups
